## The workshop

The Advanced Training Design Workshop is a small, annual working conference for people who train law enforcement and tactical professionals. Roughly 60 people attend: working trainers, tactical practitioners, and training-science researchers, all in one room for two full days of hands-on sessions. The 2026 theme is **Designing Training That Transfers**.

The workshop grew out of the ALERRT Center's ongoing ecological dynamics seminar series, which brings training-science researchers and practitioners together around how people actually learn, perceive, and decide under pressure. The workshop keeps that spirit but widens the door: no particular theoretical school is required. Presenters show their method live, explain why they do it that way, and the room takes it from there.

## The host

The workshop is hosted by the [ALERRT Center](https://alerrt.org) (Advanced Law Enforcement Rapid Response Training) at Texas State University in San Marcos, Texas. ALERRT was created in 2002 and serves as the national standard in active shooter response training, alongside an active research program on law enforcement training and performance.

## The venue

The workshop is held at [TBarM Resort](https://www.tbarm.com) in New Braunfels, Texas, on the Guadalupe River between San Antonio and Austin. Everything happens on site: sessions, meals, and lodging. See the [attend page](attend.qmd) for cost and travel details, and the [program](program.qmd) for what is on in 2026.

## Presenting

Presenters are selected through an annual call for presentations, usually posted in the spring with proposals due in early June. Selected presenters have their conference fee, room, board, and travel covered. The 2026 call has closed; the [presenting page](call-for-presentations.qmd) explains what a proposal includes, and the 2027 call will be posted there when it opens.
